solution:
**(C)** Gibberellins

Application of gibberellins overcomes the requirement of vernalization, so a plant that needs a cold treatment can be made to flower without it. Auxin mainly causes cell elongation, cytokinin promotes cell division, and ethylene ripens fruit and generally retards flowering, so none of them substitutes for chilling.

**(C)** Xylem

Water with dissolved minerals moves up the plant through the lumen of the xylem elements, the tracheids and vessels, carried along the transpiration stream. Sieve cells and sieve tube elements belong to the phloem, which carries food, so neither they nor "xylem and phloem" together is the pathway for water.

[Note: this chapter mentions minerals moving with water in the xylem but does not state the water pathway itself; standard biology (and the previous chapter on plant water relations) gives xylem as the path of ascent of sap.]

**(B)** leaf fall and dormancy

Abscisic acid promotes abscission of leaves and induces and controls dormancy in buds and seeds, which is how it got its earlier names abscisin and dormin. It inhibits cell division and cell elongation rather than controlling them, and shoot elongation is the striking effect of gibberellins.

**(B)** Ethylene

Ethylene is the gaseous hormone that promotes ripening of fruits such as bananas, apples and mangoes, and it also degreens bananas by activating chlorophyllase. Commercially it is supplied as ethephon, which releases ethylene in water. Auxin, cytokinin and gibberellin do not ripen fruit.

**(B)** Definite photoperiod

Garner and Allard found that temperature, nutrition and soil moisture did not regulate flowering, but exposure to a specific duration of light did; this is photoperiodism. Oxygen, water and minerals are needed for growth in general, but they are not the stimulus that starts flowering.

**(B)** dark/ night

Short day plants are really long night plants: they need a long uninterrupted dark period to flower, and even a flash of light during the night stops flowering. So the critical period for them is the dark period, not the light period, and ultraviolet rays play no part in the photoperiodic response.

As printed this question has three correct options: the chapter lists tomato, cotton and sunflower all as day neutral plants.

Tomato, cotton and sunflower flower throughout the year regardless of day length, which the chapter gives as examples of day neutral plants alongside cucumber, maize and balsam. Soybean (*Glycine max*) is the only option that is not day neutral: the chapter lists it as a short day plant. A question asking which one is NOT day neutral would have soybean as its single answer.

**(C)** absorbed from soil

Green plants obtain the inorganic elements they need from the soil in the form of minerals, absorbed in ionic form mainly through the roots. Plants cannot make elements: photosynthesis, enzymes and hormones only build compounds out of elements already taken in.

**(B)** biosynthesis of 3-IAA

Zinc activates various enzymes, including carboxylases, carbonic anhydrase and the dehydrogenases needed for auxin synthesis, and auxin is indole-3-acetic acid (IAA). Stomatal closing is linked with potassium movement, and chlorophyll synthesis depends on elements such as magnesium, nitrogen and iron.

**(B)** death of tissue

Necrosis is the localized death of tissue of leaves, a symptom of mineral deficiency. Yellowing of leaves is chlorosis, and wilting comes from loss of turgidity, not from tissue death.

**(D)** denitrification

In denitrification, anaerobic bacteria such as *Pseudomonas denitrificans* convert soil nitrates through nitrites and oxides of nitrogen back into nitrogen gas. Nitrification is the opposite direction (ammonia to nitrite to nitrate), ammonification turns organic nitrogen into ammonia, and nitrogen fixation turns \(\text{N}_2\) into usable compounds.

**(D)** 16

Biological nitrogen fixation is a high energy process: nitrogen fixers use 16 molecules of ATP to reduce one molecule of nitrogen to ammonia, as in \(\text{N}_2 + 8\text{H}^+ + 8e^- + 16\,\text{ATP} \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2 + 16\,\text{ADP} + 16\,\text{P}_i\).
